title: Noetherian topological spaces have no cohomology above their dimension
statement: Let X be a Noetherian topological space (every nonempty set of closed subsets of X has a minimal element for inclusion), let d\geq 0 be an integer such that the topological Krull dimension of X [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] satisfies \dim X\leq d (this includes X empty, of dimension -\infty), and let F be an abelian sheaf on X. Then H^q(X,F) [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology] is zero for every integer q>d.

proof.text: We induct on d. If X is empty, the sheaf axiom for the empty cover makes every cohomology group vanish, so the assertion is immediate. The d=0 case is handled in the irreducible step below.

source.place: Proposition 02UZ, induction on d, including the empty space

proof.text: For fixed d, induct on the finite number of irreducible components of X, using [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components]. The open-closed short exact sequence [lem-sc-noetherian-open-closed-cohomology-sequence] and the long exact sequence in [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology] reduce the assertion for a union of components to a proper closed subspace and a space with fewer components, so it suffices to treat irreducible X.

Assume X irreducible. If d=0, X has no nonempty proper open: otherwise a nonempty proper closed subset has an irreducible component Z' and Z'\subsetneq X gives a chain of irreducible closed subsets, contradicting dimension zero. Thus every abelian sheaf F is the constant sheaf with value F(X), as in the 02UZ proof, and [lem-sc-irreducible-noetherian-constant-acyclic] gives H^q(X,F)=0 for q>0. Now assume d>0. Since X is Noetherian, every subset is quasi-compact, so X is quasi-compact, quasi-compact opens form a basis, and intersections of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact; these verify hypotheses (1)-(3) of [lem-sc-noetherian-extension-by-zero-reduction].

It remains to verify hypothesis (4) of [lem-sc-noetherian-extension-by-zero-reduction]. Let j:U\to X be quasi-compact open. If U is empty, j_!Z_U=0. If U is nonempty, irreducibility makes U dense; with Z=X\setminus U, Z is a proper closed Noetherian subspace and dim Z\leq d-1, since any chain in Z extends by X. Applying [lem-sc-noetherian-open-closed-cohomology-sequence] to F=Z_X gives 0\to j_!Z_U\to Z_X\to i_*Z_Z\to0 (j^*Z_X=Z_U and i^*Z_X=Z_Z). For p>d, H^p(X,Z_X)=0 by [lem-sc-irreducible-noetherian-constant-acyclic], while H^{p-1}(X,i_*Z_Z)=H^{p-1}(Z,Z_Z)=0 by [lem-sc-cohomology-closed-immersion-pushforward] and the outer induction hypothesis applied to Z (p-1>d-1\geq\dim Z). The exact segment H^{p-1}(X,i_*Z_Z)\to H^p(X,j_!Z_U)\to H^p(X,Z_X) of the long exact sequence from [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology] therefore gives H^p(X,j_!Z_U)=0.

All four hypotheses of [lem-sc-noetherian-extension-by-zero-reduction] now hold, so it gives H^p(X,F)=0 for every p>d and every abelian sheaf F on irreducible X. The inner induction on components and then the outer induction on d complete the proof.
